events.category: Contemporary Japanese jazz / piano trio with string quartet / original arrangements
events.factual_description: COTTON CLUB presents Martha Kato Trio with Strings on January 6, 2027, as a single show opening at 18:30 and starting at 19:30. Kato's trio with Kumpei Nakabayashi and Kan is joined by violinists Atsuki Yoshida and Natsumi Okimasu, violist Kano Tajima and cellist Yumi Shimazu. The venue says newly written arrangements for this performance will recast Kato's original music. Listed per-person charges range from ¥7,700 to ¥10,200 depending on seating; member reservations open December 1 at noon and general reservations open December 7 at noon, both online.

en.why_it_matters: Kato is not simply adding generic strings to a club date. Her established trio becomes a compact seven-player ensemble, with two violins, viola and cello carrying arrangements written for this performance around her own compositions. The combination promises chamber-level color without giving up the trio's rhythmic identity, and the one-show format makes the configuration unusually focused.
en.trip_verdict: If a Tokyo stay includes January 6, actively make room for this one-off ensemble: it is a stronger reason to choose the night than a routine trio return. The evidence supports prioritizing the show, but not treating it as a historically unrepeatable occasion.

es.why_it_matters: Kato no se limita a añadir cuerdas genéricas a una fecha de club. Su trío estable se convierte en un ensamble compacto de siete músicos, con dos violines, viola y violonchelo trabajando arreglos escritos para esta función sobre sus propias composiciones. La combinación promete color de cámara sin perder la identidad rítmica del trío, y el formato de una sola función concentra la propuesta.
es.trip_verdict: Si una estancia en Tokio incluye el 6 de enero, vale la pena hacerle espacio a este ensamble de una sola noche: ofrece una razón más fuerte para elegir la fecha que un regreso rutinario del trío. La evidencia justifica priorizarlo, no tratarlo como una ocasión históricamente irrepetible.
